### 💡 Codex Review Here are some automated review suggestions for this pull request. **Reviewed commit:** `02af345db4`
ℹ️ About Codex in GitHub
Codex has been enabled to automatically review pull requests in this repo. Reviews are triggered when you - Open a pull request for review - Mark a draft as ready - Comment "@codex review". If Codex has suggestions, it will comment; otherwise it will react with 👍. When you [sign up for Codex through ChatGPT](https://openai.com/codex), Codex can also answer questions or update the PR, like "@codex address that feedback".

Hey @pcbeingused333, thank you for your contribution!

The fix is in the right place, and keeping the sync transaction path out of scope is correct. Two changes before merging:

1. Please remove the option in place with `cmd.kwargs.pop("keys", None)` instead of building a new dict. This matches the other execution paths (`redis/asyncio/client.py` transaction handling and `redis/cluster.py`) and avoids an extra allocation per command in every transaction. Nothing reads `keys` after the callbacks run.
2. Please replace the mocked test with a real-cluster test in `tests/test_asyncio/test_cluster_transaction.py`, for example `hset` a hash and then `hgetall` it inside `pipeline(transaction=True)`. The CI matrix runs that file with RESP2 and RESP3 and both response shapes, and the test does not depend on private strategy internals.
Thanks for the quick update, both points are addressed. The in-place `pop` matches the other execution paths, and the real-cluster test covers the failing RESP2 path in the CI matrix. LGTM.

review_comments.body:
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Mirror callback handling in synchronous cluster transactions**

For `RedisCluster(..., protocol=2).pipeline(transaction=True)`, the sync `TransactionStrategy` at `redis/cluster.py:6566-6574` still applies only `cluster_response_callbacks`; it never applies the ordinary `HGETALL` callback that this async branch now completes successfully. Consequently the same queued `hgetall` returns a raw `[b'a', b'1']` in sync while returning `{b'a': b'1'}` in async, so mirror the ordinary callback/options handling in the sync transaction path.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L146-L149](https://github.com/redis/redis-py/blob/02af345db472cd8c684334c951ecda88f9147437/AGENTS.md#L146-L149)

Thanks @petyaslavova, both done in 98210c6 (new commit on the branch):

1. The `keys` option is now removed in place with `cmd.kwargs.pop("keys", None)` before the callback runs, like the other execution paths.
2. The mocked test is gone from `tests/test_asyncio/test_cluster.py`. `tests/test_asyncio/test_cluster_transaction.py` has a real-cluster test instead: `hset` a hash and `hgetall` it inside `pipeline(transaction=True)`, expecting `[2, {b"a": b"1", b"b": b"2"}]`.

The new test passes with RESP2 and RESP3 against a local 6-node cluster, and fails on the previous code with `TypeError: <lambda>() got an unexpected keyword argument 'keys'` under RESP2. The full `test_cluster_transaction.py` passes there as well.
